svg.title: A-400 South Elevation — Scheme A “Wave”
svg.text: 1.95 m DEEPEST · 0.75 m SHALLOWEST · 12.8 m² A FLOOR
THE BALCONY CURVE IN PLAN — IT CANNOT SHOW IN ELEVATION
Masonry wall cut by section — 200 mm
Internal stud or block partition, 120 mm
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
in the underside of the nosing
1. The exterior only. The plans, site plan and section are
agreed and re-issued at P18 to the adopted curve; nothing
here changes the rest of them: same five levels, same 9.50
× 13.50 m footprint, same 1.00 m setbacks, same openings.
Only the skin differs between the schemes.
2. Every opening drawn here is read from the plan it belongs
to rather than redrawn, and checks.py fails the build if
an elevation ever shows one the plan does not have.
3. Scheme A takes its material from the contemporary
reference: warm limestone render, a rounded slab nosing
with a cove light tucked into its underside, clear glass
balustrades and planting along the balcony edge. The four
south bays read as glazed ribbons between the slabs.
4. The balcony curve is a serpentine — one full period across
the frontage, 1.95 m deep at each end drawn in to 0.75 m
at the waist. At the waist it is a planting ledge rather
than somewhere to stand; the deep ends carry the
5. This is the adopted curve, and the plans are drawn to it.
It cost area to take: 12.8 m² a floor against the 17.4 m²
of the curve it replaced, 18 m² over the four balcony
levels. A-000 and A-100 to A-104 are re-issued at P18 to
6. The balconies do not wrap the corner as the reference
does: the 1.00 m setbacks forbid anything projecting west,
north or east, so the cantilever stays on the street
Preliminary design issue — not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
